on_record.summary: Dulux Australia, part of DuluxGroup, which Nippon Paint owns, is listed as a sponsor.

record_funding: Creative Victoria and Creative Australia, with the City of Melbourne and the Ian Potter Foundation. Corporate partners include Dulux, KWM, Wood Marsh, Supernormal and Hannah St Hotel.

on_record.summary: Dulux is a 2026 partner. In Indonesia it is an AkzoNobel joint venture that Nippon Paint agreed in October 2026 to buy.

record_funding: Run since 2024 by Majelis Jakarta, which the Jakarta Arts Council set up; the Creative Economy Ministry offered its support in 2026.

on_record.summary: Dulux is listed as a partner. In Pakistan it is the brand of Akzo Nobel Pakistan, which AkzoNobel sold to the Packages Group in September 2026.

record_funding: Punjab and federal government bodies fund it. Habib Bank is lead sponsor, with Barjeel Art Foundation, Bareeze and ICCI as star sponsors and Nishat, PIA, Dulux and Careem as partners.

on_record.summary: Dulux New Zealand, owned by Nippon Paint through DuluxGroup, was listed as a current sponsor on the museum’s Partner with us page in January 2025.

record_funding: Mostly funded by Hutt City Council, plus the Dowse Foundation; Jan 2025 archive names Dulux as a corporate partner and Steel & Tube as a donor.

on_record.summary: Bouygues Bâtiment Sud-Est is among the patrons (mécènes) the biennale lists for 2026.

record_funding: Its site lists four public partners, the Ministère de la Culture, the Région Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, the Métropole de Lyon and the Ville de Lyon, then Groupe Partouche, Grand Casino de Lyon Le Pharaon as 'partenaire historique', Esker as 'mécène officiel' and Société Générale and LPA Mobilités as 'mécènes associés'. The pages read did not state amounts.

on_record.summary: Bouygues Bâtiment Nord-Est is a member of the Cercle Louvre-Lens, the museum's patrons' club.

record_funding: Its statutes split the cost between the Région Hauts-de-France (8/10), the Département du Pas-de-Calais (1/10) and the Communauté d'Agglomération Lens-Liévin (1/10): 9 991 840 €, 1 061 650 € and 1 248 980 € in 2025. The state pays 500 K€ a year under a three-year agreement, tickets brought 1,08 M€ and patronage and space hire 873 K€ in 2025, with 150 K€ from Crédit Mutuel and 100 K€ from AXA for exhibitions (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).

on_record.summary: Leonard Lauder’s 2008 gift of $131 million, the largest in the museum’s history.

record_funding: Admissions, board patron gifts, Hyundai Motor.

on_record.summary: Eva and Glenn Dubin are listed among PS1 Benefactors in MoMA's 2023-24 report; he is a MoMA trustee.

record_funding: Subsidiary of The Museum of Modern Art; supported by NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, MoMA Board, and foundation grants.

on_record.summary: A Leadership Circle donor, as NNPC Seplat Energy.

record_funding: First partners: Edo State Government, Germany's Foreign Office, Mellon Foundation, British Museum, PI Trust. Leadership Circle donors include NNPC Seplat Energy, Lekoil Nigeria and Azura Power West Africa.

on_record.summary: Pheroza and Jamshyd Godrej are donors of Rs 50 lakh and above, and the Pirojsha Godrej Foundation of Rs 25 lakh and above, since 1995.

record_funding: An autonomous institution, by its own account un-aided by government. Donors of Rs 10 crore and above: Ministry of Culture, Citibank, Bank of America, TCS Foundation, J. Paul Getty Trust.

on_record.summary: Freelands Foundation, set up by Elisabeth Murdoch in 2015, is among its funders.

record_funding: £863k income (FY2025); ACE NPO, Freelands Fdn (Murdoch media money), Garfield Weston, Art Fund, local councils, Thalia Waste.

on_record.summary: The Crown Resorts Foundation is listed among NGV Foundation donors (annual report 2024/25).

record_funding: Year to June 2025: government core grants $89.5M, commercial revenue $62.7M. Partners include Mercedes-Benz, MECCA, Telstra, Country Road, Deakin University, Macquarie Group, Qantas, HSBC Australia and EY.

on_record.summary: One of three current Gallery Partners.

record_funding: Dunedin City Council gallery. Gallery Partners are Creative New Zealand, Quartz Reef and Craigs Investment Partners; the DPAG Society buys works.

on_record.summary: A listed supporter of the UK Antarctic Heritage Trust, which runs the site; its cruise passengers are most of the visitors.

record_funding: Run by the UK Antarctic Heritage Trust, which took £1.65M in the year to April 2025: £927,850 from its shops and £715,974 from donations, membership and grants. HX and Quark are listed supporters.

on_record.summary: The family is one of the museum’s three founding partners on its patrons page.

record_funding: Ferré-Rangel and Fonalledas families, Fundación Ángel Ramos, 700+ individuals. Gala sponsors: Banco Popular, Genera PR (New Fortress Energy, 2023), Puma Energy (2019). 2024-25 Form 990: government grants 58%, earnings <1%.
